Order 
This is the first application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C.) for grant of anticipatory bail, filed on behalf of the applicants, who apprehend their arrest in connection with Crime No. 84/2024 registered at Police Station Mihona, District Bhind (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 506 of IPC added section 323, 201 of IPC.
2.

As per the prosecution story, on 08.10.2023, when the husband of the prosecutrix had gone to the market, co-accused Neeraj Kushwah came to her house and allegedly committed forcible sexual intercourse with her.
The prosecutrix alleged that Neeraj threatened to kill her husband if she disclosed the incident to anyone.
Taking advantage of opportunities, Neeraj is alleged to have committed rape on multiple occasions.

On 23.06.2024, when Neeraj NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24393 2 MCRC-42955-2025 again attempted to outrage her modesty, the husband of the prosecutrix arrived, whereafter the prosecutrix narrated the entire incident.
Based on her complaint, Crime No. 84/2024 was registered.

In her supplementary statement, the prosecutrix alleged that on 05.09.2024 after lodging present FIR while coming out of the police station along with her husband and brother, co-accused Neeraj along with present applicants Nitesh and Narendra assaulted and quarreled with them.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that the applicants are innocent and have been falsely implicated as the allegation of assaulting the prosecutrix and her husband while they were returning from Police Station after lodging the FIR appears to be an afterthought.

It is contended that in the FIR the name of the present applicants did not figure at all and the specific allegation of rape is against co-accused Neeraj alone, who has already been granted the benefit of anticipatory bail by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Special Leave to Appeal (Criminal) No. 14632/2024 by order dated 27.11.2024.

It is further submitted that the applicants were earlier granted regular bail by the trial Court but due to their absence on subsequent dates of hearing, non-bailable warrants were issued against them.
Learned counsel submitted that the applicants are willing to cooperate in the investigation and abide by all conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the application and prayed for its dismissal.

5. Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.

Considering the overall circumstances of the case and the fact NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24393 3 MCRC-42955-2025 that the allegation of rape is specifically attributed to co-accused Neeraj who has already been extended the benefit of anticipatory bail by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, without commenting upon the merits of the matter, this Court finds it appropriate to extend the benefit of anticipatory bail to the applicants.
7. Accordingly, the application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicants Narendra Singh Kushwah and Nitesh Kushwah shall be released on anticipatory bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) each with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer/Investigating Officer.

4. The applicants shall not commit any offence during the period of bail;
5.

9. Application stands allowed and disposed of.
10. Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court/Police Station concerned for compliance.
